description: This course, offered by the Department of Computer Engineering, focuses on building robust applications using Python programming, and building multithreaded, platform-independent and GUI based Python applications for business problems.

syllabus.title: The Concept of Data Types
syllabus.body: Variables, Assignments; Immutable Variables; Numerical Types; Arithmetic Operators And Expressions; comments in the program; understanding error messages; Conditions, boolean logic, logical operators; ranges; Control statements: if-else, loops (for, while); short-circuit (lazy) evaluation; Strings and text files; manipulating files and directories, os and sys modules; text files: reading/writing text and numbers from/to a file; creating and reading a formatted file (csv or tab-separated); String manipulations: subscript operator, indexing, slicing a string.

syllabus.title: Lists, Tuples, and Dictionaries
syllabus.body: Basic list operators, replacing, inserting, removing an element; searching and sorting lists; dictionary literals, adding and removing keys, accessing and replacing values; traversing dictionaries; Design with functions: hiding redundancy, complexity; arguments and return values; formal vs actual arguments, named arguments.

syllabus.title: Simple Graphics, Image Processing and OOP
syllabus.body: "turtle" module; simple 2d drawing - colors, shapes; digital images, image file formats, image processing: Simple image manipulations with 'image' module (convert to bw, greyscale, blur, etc). Classes and OOP: classes, objects, attributes and methods; defining classes; design with classes, data modeling; persistent storage of objects; inheritance, polymorphism, operator overloading (_eq_, _str_, etc); abstract classes; exception handling, try block.

syllabus.title: Graphical User Interfaces
syllabus.body: Event-driven programming paradigm; tkinter module, creating simple GUI; buttons, labels, entry fields, dialogs; widget attributes - sizes, fonts, colors layouts, nested frames.

outcomes: Programming ability for solving simple business problems.
Design of robust and multithreaded python applications.
referenceBooks: T.R. Padmanabhan, Programming with Python, Springer, 1st Ed., 2016.
Kenneth Lambert, Fundamentals of Python: First Programs, Cengage Learning, 1st Ed., 2012.
